44533: Archbishop James Ussher, Annales Veteris Testamenti (1650)
44535: Old-earth readings: no datable year (cosmos c. 13.8 billion years)
44537: God creates the heavens and the earth, and forms the man and woman in his image and places them in Eden. Genesis gives no calendar date; the year shown follows the Masoretic genealogies as summed by Ussher and is a placeholder only. Many interpreters do not read Genesis 1 as giving a datable chronology at all.
44539: Adam and Eve eat from the forbidden tree, are judged, and are sent out of Eden; God promises that the woman's offspring will strike the serpent's head. No date is recoverable from the text.
44541: Cain kills his brother Abel and is driven out as a wanderer; Seth is born in Abel's place and people begin to call on the name of the LORD.
44543: Enoch "walked with God, and he was not, for God took him." Hebrews reads this as being taken without seeing death. The year follows the Masoretic genealogy and is not secure.
44545: Regional-flood readings: undatable, sometimes linked to Mesopotamian floods c. 2900 BC
44546: God judges a violent world by flood, preserves Noah's family and the animals in the ark, and makes a covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood. The ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Readers differ on date and on whether the flood was global or regional.
44548: Humanity gathers in the plain of Shinar to build a city and tower; God confuses their language and scatters them. The setting recalls Mesopotamian ziggurats. No date is given.
44550: Early (Masoretic, 1 Kgs 6:1 + Exod 12:40 = 430 years in Egypt)
44551: Shorter sojourn (215 years in Egypt per LXX Exod 12:40)
44552: Middle Bronze II setting favoured by many archaeologists
44554: God calls Abram out of Haran (having first left Ur with Terah) and promises land, offspring and blessing for all families of the earth. At Shechem God promises the land to his offspring and Abram builds an altar.
44558: Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister; Pharaoh is struck with plagues and sends them away. They return through the Negev to Bethel.
44560: After Abram rescues Lot from four eastern kings, Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine and blesses him; Abram gives him a tenth.
44561: Abram believes the LORD and it is counted to him as righteousness. God passes between the halves of the animals and swears to give the land, foretelling four hundred years of affliction for Abram's offspring.
44563: At Sarai's urging Abram has a son by Hagar the Egyptian. Hagar flees and meets the angel of the LORD, whom she names "the God who sees me." Abram is 86.
44565: Abraham intercedes for Sodom; the cities of the plain are destroyed, Lot is rescued and his wife looks back.
44567: Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is a hundred years old, as God had promised.
44568: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac on a mountain in the land of Moriah, then stops him and provides a ram. Chronicles places the later temple on Mount Moriah.
44570: After taking Esau's blessing by deception, Jacob flees toward Haran; at Bethel he dreams of a stairway to heaven and God renews the Abrahamic promise to him.
44572: Returning from Paddan-aram with his family, Jacob wrestles through the night with a man at the Jabbok, is renamed Israel, and limps away blessed.
44574: Joseph's brothers throw him into a pit at Dothan and sell him to traders bound for Egypt, where he is sold to Potiphar.
44577: After interpreting Pharaoh's dreams of plenty and famine, Joseph at thirty is set over the land of Egypt and stores grain.
44579: Early chronology (430 years before a 1446 exodus)
44580: Late chronology (430 years before a 1260 exodus)
44581: Jacob, at 130, brings seventy persons of his household to Egypt, is reunited with Joseph, and settles in Goshen.
44583: Hammurabi of Babylon (reigned c. 1792–1750 BC, middle chronology) unifies much of Mesopotamia and issues his law code, a frequent comparison point for the covenant laws of Exodus.
44586: Ahmose I drives the Hyksos out of the Delta and founds the Eighteenth Dynasty, opening Egypt's imperial New Kingdom. Some link a "new king who did not know Joseph" (Exod 1:8) to this shift.
44589: A new Pharaoh fears Israel's growth, sets taskmasters over them to build store cities Pithom and Raamses, and orders the Hebrew baby boys killed.
44592: Jochebed hides her son in a basket among the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter adopts him and names him Moses.
44594: Tending Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses meets God in a bush that burns without being consumed, learns the divine name "I AM WHO I AM," and is sent to Pharaoh.
44595: Early exodus (1 Kgs 6:1: 480 years before 966 BC)
44597: After ten plagues and the first Passover, Israel leaves Rameses for Succoth. The date is one of the most debated in biblical chronology: 1 Kings 6:1 points to c. 1446 BC, while the city name Rameses and the archaeology of Canaan lead many to c. 1260 BC under Ramesses II. A minority deny a historical mass exodus.
44598: The LORD divides the sea (Hebrew yam suph, "Sea of Reeds") and Israel crosses on dry ground; Pharaoh's chariots are drowned. Moses and Miriam sing. The location is disputed (Gulf of Suez, Bitter Lakes, Gulf of Aqaba, or a northern lagoon).
44599: In the third month Israel camps before Sinai; God speaks the Ten Commandments and the covenant is ratified with blood.
44600: While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes a golden calf. Moses breaks the tablets, intercedes, and the covenant is renewed with God revealing himself as merciful and gracious.
44602: On the first day of the second year the tabernacle is raised and the glory of the LORD fills it; Aaron and his sons are ordained.
44604: Ten of twelve spies discourage the people; only Joshua and Caleb urge trust. The generation is sentenced to forty years in the wilderness.
44608: From Mount Nebo Moses sees the promised land, dies in Moab at 120, and is buried by God; Joshua succeeds him.
44612: The Jordan stops while the priests carry the ark across; Israel camps at Gilgal. Jericho's walls fall after seven days of marching and Rahab's household is spared. Archaeologists dispute whether Jericho was occupied in either proposed period.
44613: Joshua gathers the tribes at Shechem and calls them to choose whom they will serve: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
44615: Israel serves the Baals and is oppressed; the LORD raises up Othniel, Caleb's nephew, and the land has rest forty years. This begins the cycle of the judges.
44617: Clay-tablet correspondence between Pharaoh and Canaanite city-kings (including Jerusalem's Abdi-Heba) complains of the troublesome Habiru. Some link Habiru with Hebrews; most scholars see a broader social term.
44619: Ramesses II fights the Hittite king Muwatalli II at Kadesh on the Orontes, the best-documented chariot battle of antiquity; a peace treaty follows c. 1259 BC.
44621: Deborah the prophetess summons Barak; from Mount Tabor Israel routs Jabin's general Sisera by the Kishon, and Jael kills Sisera. The Song of Deborah is among the oldest Hebrew poems.
44623: Pharaoh Merneptah's victory inscription lists "Israel" as a people in Canaan, the earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel.
44624: Sea Peoples and the Bronze Age collapse
44625: Across the eastern Mediterranean palace civilizations collapse; Ramesses III repels the Sea Peoples, among them the Peleset, who settle the coastal plain as the Philistine pentapolis.
44627: Gideon, reluctant and testing God with a fleece, defeats the Midianites with three hundred men bearing trumpets and torches.
44629: The outcast Jephthah defeats Ammon but is bound by a rash vow concerning his daughter; interpreters still debate what he did.
44633: In the days of the judges, Ruth the Moabite clings to Naomi, marries Boaz of Bethlehem, and becomes great-grandmother of David.
44635: Hannah dedicates her son to the LORD; the boy Samuel hears God's voice at night in the Shiloh sanctuary and becomes a recognized prophet.
44637: Samson the Nazirite fights the Philistines, is betrayed by Delilah, and dies pulling down the temple of Dagon at Gaza.
44638: Ark captured at Aphek; Eli dies
44639: The Philistines defeat Israel and capture the ark; Eli's sons die and Eli falls dead at the news. The ark brings plague on the Philistine cities and is returned.
44641: Israel asks for a king "like all the nations." Samuel anoints Saul of Benjamin, who is publicly chosen by lot at Mizpah. The regnal figure in 1 Sam 13:1 is textually damaged, so his dates are approximate.
44643: After rejecting Saul, the LORD sends Samuel to Jesse's house, where the youngest son, David, is anointed and the Spirit rushes upon him.
44645: In the Valley of Elah the shepherd David kills the Philistine champion Goliath of Gath with a sling stone, declaring the battle is the LORD's.
44647: The Philistines defeat Israel at Gilboa; Saul and Jonathan die. David laments them in the Song of the Bow.
44650: Judah anoints David king at Hebron, where he reigns seven and a half years before all Israel makes him king.
44652: David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion, makes it his capital, and brings the ark up with dancing. The Tel Dan inscription (9th c. BC) later refers to the "House of David."
44653: Through Nathan, God promises to build David a "house" and establish his offspring's throne forever, a promise later read messianically.
44655: David takes Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death; Nathan confronts him with a parable and David repents.
44656: Absalom proclaims himself king at Hebron; David flees over the Mount of Olives. Absalom is killed by Joab and David mourns him.
44658: Solomon is anointed at Gihon to forestall Adonijah; at Gibeon he asks God for wisdom.
44660: In Solomon's fourth year, "the 480th year after Israel came out of Egypt," work begins on the temple on Mount Moriah. This verse is the anchor for the early exodus date.
44662: The ark is brought into the Most Holy Place, the cloud of glory fills the house, and Solomon prays for Israel and the foreigner.
44664: The queen of Sheba (probably southern Arabia) tests Solomon with hard questions and praises his God.
44665: At Shechem Rehoboam refuses to lighten Solomon's yoke; the ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king. Judah and Benjamin remain with the house of David.
44667: To keep his people from going to Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and appoints his own priests and feasts, "the sin of Jeroboam" that Kings condemns in every northern reign.
44669: In Rehoboam's fifth year Pharaoh Shishak takes the treasures of the temple. Shoshenq I's relief at Karnak lists towns he campaigned against; a fragment of his stele was found at Megiddo.
44671: Omri moves the northern capital from Tirzah to the hill of Samaria. Assyrian records continue to call Israel "the house of Omri" long after his dynasty fell; the Mesha Stele names him too.
44673: Jehoshaphat of Judah sends Levites to teach the Book of the Law in the cities and appoints judges, while allying with Ahab by marriage.
44674: After a three-year drought, Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal on Carmel; fire falls on the LORD's altar and the people cry, "The LORD, he is God."
44675: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah travels forty days to Horeb, hears the LORD not in wind, earthquake or fire but in "a low whisper," and is sent to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha.
44677: Shalmaneser III of Assyria fights a coalition of western kings at Qarqar on the Orontes. His Kurkh Monolith credits "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots, the first extra-biblical mention of an Israelite king by name. The Bible does not mention the battle.
44678: Micaiah's warning; Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
44679: After Ahab seizes Naboth's vineyard, the lone prophet Micaiah foretells his death; Ahab is killed by a random arrow at Ramoth-gilead.
44680: Elijah is taken to heaven in a whirlwind with chariots of fire; Elisha picks up his cloak and receives a double portion of his spirit.
44681: The Aramean commander Naaman washes seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word and is cleansed of leprosy.
44683: Anointed at Elisha's command, Jehu kills Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah and Jezebel, and purges Baal worship. Shalmaneser III's Black Obelisk shows "Jehu son of Omri" bowing with tribute.
44684: King Mesha of Moab records his revolt against Israel and names Omri and the God of Israel (YHWH); it parallels the Moabite rebellion in 2 Kings 3.
44686: Athaliah, Ahab's daughter, murders the royal heirs of Judah, but the infant Joash is hidden in the temple; after six years the priest Jehoiada crowns him.
44690: Jonah son of Amittai, a prophet under Jeroboam II, flees from his call, is swallowed by a great fish, and preaches to Nineveh, which repents. Readers differ on whether the book is historical narrative or a parable-like story.
44692: Amos, a herdsman of Tekoa, denounces Israel's injustice "two years before the earthquake" in the prosperous days of Jeroboam II.
44694: Hosea is told to marry Gomer, whose unfaithfulness pictures Israel's; he proclaims God's jealous, persistent love.
44696: Tiglath-pileser III (called Pul) reorganizes Assyria into a standing empire and deports conquered peoples; Menahem pays him tribute and he later annexes Galilee.
44698: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD high and lifted up and hears the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy."
44700: Aram and Israel attack Judah to force it into an anti-Assyrian alliance. Isaiah offers Ahaz the sign of Immanuel; Ahaz instead buys Assyrian help, and Damascus falls in 732 BC.
44701: Micah warns that Zion will be plowed like a field and foretells a ruler from Bethlehem; a century later Jeremiah's defenders cite him.
44702: After a three-year siege Samaria falls to Assyria (Shalmaneser V, with Sargon II claiming the deportation of 27,290 people). The northern kingdom ends; Kings explains it as the fruit of covenant unfaithfulness.
44706: Hezekiah removes the high places, breaks the bronze serpent, cleanses the temple and holds a great Passover inviting northerners too.
44708: Sennacherib devastates Judah and takes Lachish (shown on his palace reliefs at Nineveh). His annals boast he shut Hezekiah up "like a bird in a cage" but do not claim Jerusalem's capture; the Bible records the Assyrian army struck down and Sennacherib's withdrawal.
44710: Hezekiah channels the Gihon spring into the city; the Siloam Inscription describes the two crews of tunnelers meeting.
44712: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sheds much innocent blood; Chronicles adds his captivity and repentance. Kings names him the decisive cause of the exile.
44714: In Josiah's thirteenth year the young priest's son from Anathoth is appointed "a prophet to the nations."
44715: Book of the Law found; Josiah's reform
44716: Repairs to the temple uncover the Book of the Law; the prophetess Huldah confirms its warnings, and Josiah purges idolatry as far as Bethel and keeps a great Passover.
44718: Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh, as Nahum and Zephaniah had announced; the Assyrian remnant retreats to Haran.
44720: Josiah confronts Pharaoh Necho II, marching north to aid Assyria, and is killed at Megiddo. Jeremiah laments him.
44722: Crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crushes Necho's Egyptian army at Carchemish on the Euphrates, making Babylon master of the Levant. The Babylonian Chronicle confirms the date.
44725: Critical: stories composed later; book finalized c. 165 BC
44726: Nebuchadnezzar takes young nobles, including Daniel and his three friends, to be trained in Babylon. Dan 1:1 dates this to Jehoiakim's third year.
44729: Daniel interprets the king's dream of a statue of four metals struck by a stone that becomes a mountain filling the earth.
44731: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem on 16 March 597 BC (Babylonian Chronicle), exiles King Jehoiachin with ten thousand leading citizens, and sets Zedekiah on the throne.
44733: By the Chebar canal the priest Ezekiel sees the glory of God on a chariot-throne and is sent as a watchman to the exiles.
44734: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image and are delivered from the furnace with a fourth figure among them.
44737: After an eighteen-month siege Babylon breaches the walls; Zedekiah is blinded, the temple is burned and many are deported. The Lachish ostraca record the last days of Judah's defense. Some date the fall to 587 BC.
44741: The Babylonian-appointed governor Gedaliah is assassinated at Mizpah; fearing reprisal, the remnant flees to Egypt, taking Jeremiah and Baruch.
44743: Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin from prison and gives him a place at the king's table. Babylonian ration tablets list "Ya'ukin, king of Judah."
44744: Daniel's visions of the four beasts
44746: Critical: composed during Antiochus IV's persecution
44747: In Belshazzar's first year Daniel sees four beasts and "one like a son of man" receiving an everlasting kingdom. The date of the book is debated: traditionally Daniel wrote in the sixth century; many critical scholars date its final form to the Maccabean crisis c. 165 BC.
44748: Babylon falls to Cyrus; Belshazzar's feast
44749: Persian forces take Babylon in October 539 BC. Daniel reads the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. The Nabonidus Chronicle and Cyrus Cylinder describe the city's fall; Belshazzar is known as Nabonidus's co-regent son.
44750: Under "Darius the Mede," Daniel keeps praying toward Jerusalem and is delivered from the lions. The identity of Darius the Mede is itself debated (Gubaru, Cyrus under another title, or a literary figure).
44752: In his first year Cyrus permits the exiles to return and rebuild the house of God. The Cyrus Cylinder records his general policy of restoring peoples and their gods.
44754: Returnees lay the foundation; the young shout for joy while the old who remembered Solomon's temple weep. Opposition halts the work.
44755: Haggai and Zechariah stir the rebuilding
44756: In Darius I's second year, the prophets rebuke the people for paneled houses while God's house lies in ruins; work resumes.
44759: The temple is finished in Darius's sixth year (515 BC by some reckonings) and dedicated with Passover.
44761: By Roman tradition the last king is expelled and the Republic founded; Rome will dominate the Mediterranean within four centuries.
44763: Athens repels Darius I's invasion at Marathon; ten years later Xerxes' invasion fails at Salamis (480 BC).
44765: In Xerxes' (Ahasuerus') seventh year Esther becomes queen; she later risks her life to avert Haman's plot, and the Jews keep Purim.
44769: Ezra the scribe comes "in the seventh year of Artaxerxes" to teach the Law; he later reads it publicly while Levites explain the sense. Whether this was Artaxerxes I or II is debated.
44771: The king's cupbearer receives permission in Artaxerxes I's twentieth year; the walls are finished in fifty-two days despite Sanballat and Tobiah.
44773: Malachi confronts careless priests and broken marriages and promises a messenger and the return of Elijah. Jewish tradition sees prophecy ceasing after him.
44775: Alexander the Great besieges Tyre and Gaza, takes Egypt and founds Alexandria. Many read Daniel's swift he-goat as Greece. Greek language and culture spread across the east.
44776: Ptolemies and Seleucids divide the east
44777: After the battle of Ipsus Alexander's generals carve up his empire; Judea passes under the Ptolemies of Egypt until 198 BC, then the Seleucids of Syria. Daniel 11 traces "kings of the south and north."
44779: The Torah is translated into Greek in Alexandria (the Letter of Aristeas tells of seventy-two translators); the rest of the scriptures follow over the next century. The Septuagint becomes the Bible of the early church.
44781: Antiochus IV Epiphanes bans circumcision and Sabbath and sets up an altar to Zeus in the temple, the "abomination that makes desolate" of Daniel.
44783: The priest Mattathias and his sons, led by Judas Maccabeus, revolt against Seleucid rule (1 Maccabees 2–4, in the Apocrypha).
44785: Judas Maccabeus cleanses the temple and rededicates the altar, the origin of the Feast of Dedication that Jesus attended in Jerusalem.
44787: Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes emerge; a community at Qumran by the Dead Sea copies scriptures and sectarian texts later found as the Dead Sea Scrolls.
44788: Under Simon the Seleucids recognize Judean independence; the Hasmoneans rule as high priests and later kings, expanding into Idumea, Samaria and Galilee.
44789: Called in to settle a Hasmonean civil war, Pompey captures Jerusalem and enters the Holy of Holies; Judea becomes a Roman client.
44790: Herod the Great king of Judea
44791: Appointed "king of the Jews" by the Roman Senate (40 BC), Herod takes Jerusalem in 37 BC and rules as a client king.
44793: Octavian receives the title Augustus; the Pax Romana opens roads and sea lanes later used by the apostles.
44797: Herod starts a vast reconstruction of the temple and its platform; work continues into the 60s AD.
44802: Census of Quirinius AD 6 (if Luke means the known census)
44803: Jesus is born in Bethlehem in the days of Herod the Great. Because Herod died c. 4 BC (or, on a minority view, 1 BC) and Luke links the birth to a census under Quirinius, the year is debated; the traditional AD 1 rests on a sixth-century miscalculation by Dionysius Exiguus.
44807: Magi from the east worship the child; warned in a dream, Joseph takes the family to Egypt until Herod dies, then settles in Nazareth.
44811: Herod dies after a lunar eclipse and before Passover (Josephus). His kingdom is split among Archelaus, Antipas and Philip.
44812: Jesus at twelve in the temple
44815: At Passover the boy Jesus stays behind, listening and asking questions among the teachers: "I must be in my Father's house."
